data.body: WAVE 2 INSTRUMENT CHANGE APPROVED AND DELIVERED - the metric-6 miss-versus-gap partition. Owner approved a Phase-3.5 COVERAGE PANEL (standalone, n=1 with a 3-run n=3 calibration) over folding a covering_criteria field into Phase 2, after measurement showed the two cost the same (~730k vs ~650k tokens over 20 runs) while only the standalone version leaves Phase 2 untouched and can retrofit Wave 1 for ~500k instead of ~6M in re-judging. Owner also approved the Wave 1 retrofit immediately. New harness: catalogue.py (per-run criteria catalogue recovered as a committed blob at each run's own verified_at_sha - registries differ across the corpus: 43 criteria at 9bdb22f5, 42 at db2b0dc1, 45 today), coverage_pack.py, COVERAGE_INSTRUCTIONS.md, coverage_aggregate.py, coverage_report.py, coverage_state.py. RESULT over 19 pooled runs and 241 missed issues: ZERO GAPS. 231 miss/silent (96 percent), 5 miss/not-routed (2 percent), 5 miss/withdrawn (2 percent). The superseded single-judge figure was 233 misses / 3 gaps; on the panel basis the gap column is empty - every TP rebar missed is inside the remit of a criterion it already had, so recall is a detection problem not a coverage problem. Three of the four classes cost no judgement: routing and execution are read off coverage.routing and usage.per_criterion in each sidecar, separating detection failure from routing failure mechanically. Calibration answered the n=1 question: covered-vs-gap unanimity 1.000 on all three panels, exact criterion-set agreement 0.29-0.40, mean pairwise Jaccard 0.80-0.88 - the headline partition is safe at one rater, the per-criterion attribution is not. Specificity check: 207 of 241 issues covered by 2+ criteria, only 15 by exactly one (G6 most-named at 121 but sole cover on just 2), so zero-gaps is not one broad criterion absorbing everything. RESULTS.md regenerated; diff is exactly one paragraph, every other number byte-identical.
